 (WKRC) - Honda is recalling 635,808 vehicles in the United States because a software problem could disable power steering assist and make vehicles harder to steer, according to a recall report filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration .
 The recall covers certain 2021-25 Acura TLX, 2022-24 Acura MDX and 2023-25 Honda Pilot vehicles. Under certain conditions, the electronic power steering system could enter a fail-safe mode. The steering warning lights would turn on, and drivers would need to use more force to turn the wheel, potentially making the vehicle harder to control and increasing the risk of a crash. 
 The recall report lists “Do Not Drive” and “Park Outside” advisories. Owners should contact a Honda or Acura dealer for instructions. Dealers will reprogram the electronic power steering control unit with updated software at no charge. 
 Honda plans to mail letters to owners beginning Dec. 14. Owners can call Honda at 866-784-1870 for more information. The recall is listed under Honda campaign numbers KQB and TQA. 
 Honda reported 146 warranty claims and one injury report connected to the issue through Oct. 22. The company reported no deaths.
